findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: Observed mouse droppings on the floor of the dry storage area, as well as on top of unused dish racks that are stored inside of the dish room. The facility has active pest control, however, frequent cleaning should occur to eliminate harboring conditions. The floor in the dry storage area contained spilled foods, which are environments that keep insects and pests around to feed. Additionally, a dead insect was observed underneath the triple sink inside of the dish room.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the kitchen being in full operation, there wasn't a sanitizer solution present. A sanitizer solution was created and tested at 200ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer solution present if food handling, preparing, or serving is occurring.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several gallons of milk to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date in the standing cooler. The fat free milks were dated 7/19/2024 and 7/26/2024 and the 2% milk was dated 7/30/2024. Discussed with PIC and milks were pulled from the cooler and discarded. Ensure that milks never exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date and are discarded if not used within 7 days of opening. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

4-302.14: A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.citation_text: 3-304.12  (C) Observed the scoops in the flour and the sugar to be buried inside the flour and sugar. findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12 Manager was observed washing hands without proper technique. Manual faucet was shut off without a barrier prior to obtaining paper towels to dry hands. 
Also, a few times wait staff were observed using paper towels to start drying hands, then shut off the faucet, and then continued using the same paper towels to finish drying hands. 
At least one member of the wait staff was observed rushing the handwash process a few times and not doing a full 10-15 second scrubbing with soap prior to rinsing hands. Proper handwashing technique was discussed.
Management was advised to discuss proper handwashing procedure with all staff. 
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink. Use of forearms and elbows to shut off the manual faucet would also be acceptable.
findings.citation_text:

Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands must also be washed upon entering the work area, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Shell eggs had surface temperatures ranging from 41F to above 50F in a pan that was being cold held on the service line in an open top cooler. One of the shell eggs on the top layer was cracked to check the internal temperature and observed at 49F-50F. Storage practices were discussed for shell eggs during service, and ice was added to the pan of shell eggs to help maintain colder temperature. 

Sliced melon in fruit salad had internal temperatures of 44F-45F and 51F-52F depending on whether melon was in the bottom of the bowl or in the top/along upper edges. Bowl of fruit salad was held on ice during breakfast service. Proper use of ice baths for cold holding was discussed. Leftover portion of fruit salad was to be discarded at the end of breakfast service today.

Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as a public health control, cold TCS foods shall be maintained at 41°F/below.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Food thermometer used to check the hot holding temperature of sausage in the steam table appeared to be off by several degrees. Inspector's digital stem thermometer read at 138F, while the bi-metallic stem thermometer used by the facility was observed reading below 135F. Thermometer was checked in ice water and observed registering below 32F. Thermometer was calibrated to 32°F in the ice water solution. Cleaning and maintenance of food thermometers were discussed.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2°F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12 Ice scoop was observed on top of the ice machine. Top of the ice machine was soiled to the touch with some dust accumulation. Proper storage of the ice scoop between uses was discussed with staff. 
During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food preparation and dispensing utensils, such as ice scoops, shall be stored in a clean, protected location.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.13 Facility does not currently have a way other than an infrared thermometer for checking the final rinse temperature at the surface of the dishes. Options for tools that may be utilized for measuring the final rinse surface  temperature were discussed. 
In hot water mechanical warewashing operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the utensil surface temperature.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.11 & 6-501.12 Dust and general buildup were observed on the condenser surfaces and fan covers as well as on the ceiling above the condenser and around the electrical conduit leading to the light fixture in the walkin cooler. Clean the aforementioned surfaces in the walkin cooler as needed to eliminate buildup of dust and mold.

Shelving in the chemical closet was observed in various states of disrepair and were noted to no longer be easily cleanable. Sticky buildup was present in several areas, paint was peeling, and the lower shelf was held up by 5 gallon chemical buckets. Shelving needs to be replaced or repaired to allow for ease in cleaning to help maintain shelving in a sanitary condition. 
Physical facilities shall be maintained in good repair, and cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Observed can opener blade is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, saniti ze food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11  (C) Food is not protected from contamination at the 2 in place cutting boards.  Cutting boards have deep grooves and gouges, making them difficult to clean and sanitize. Food shall be protected from contamination. Reference 3-307.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed soil residue present on fans in walk in cooler. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.
